question: Should I Use the Block Editor or Switch Back to Classic?
metaDescription: The block editor is where active development is focused — worth adopting unless a specific plugin or workflow genuinely depends on Classic.
shortAnswer: The block editor (Gutenberg) is where WordPress core development is actively focused, with full-site editing, patterns, and ongoing feature work all building on it — the Classic Editor remains supported but isn't where new capability is landing. For most sites, the block editor is the right default; sticking with Classic makes sense mainly when a specific, still-actively-used plugin or an established content workflow genuinely depends on it and hasn't been migrated.

bodyHtml:
The Real Difference

Classic Editor provides a single large text area with a toolbar, similar to a word processor, while the block editor treats every piece of content — a paragraph, an image, a button, a whole section — as an individually editable and rearrangeable block. This block model is also what full-site editing, block patterns, and most new WordPress features are built on top of, which is why staying on Classic increasingly means missing out on newer capability rather than just having a different editing feel.

What to Check Before Switching

  • Plugins with deep Classic Editor integration (some older SEO or page-builder-adjacent plugins) may need checking for block editor compatibility before a full switch.
  • An established content team's workflow built entirely around Classic's interface has a real (if temporary) retraining cost worth planning for, not dismissing.
  • A site already using a full page builder (Elementor, for instance) for most content design may see less immediate benefit from switching, since the page builder handles layout regardless of which underlying editor is active.
  • The Classic Editor plugin remains officially supported for now, so there's no urgent forced-migration pressure, but new WordPress capability increasingly assumes the block editor as the default.

Making the Decision

  1. Check plugin compatibility with the block editor for anything critical to the current workflow.
  2. Trial the block editor on a staging copy with real content before committing to a full switch.
  3. Plan for a short retraining period if switching an established content team over from Classic.

Need help migrating content or workflows to the block editor smoothly? See WordPress bug fix.
